events.title: DC415
events.description: Noisebridge Hackerspace This group was created to bring together people who share a passion for cybersecurity and a curiosity about how things work. The goal is simple — to connect with other humans who enjoy meaningful, inspiring, and sometimes unexpected security conversations more than just once a year. Many of us have returned from security conferences feeling both inspired and overwhelmed — full of new ideas and projects to explore, only to have life pull us in other directions. Maybe a demanding client, a new sprint, or even a new baby shifted priorities away from that funny blinky badge project sitting on a shelf. If that sounds familiar, you’re not alone. This meetup offers a space for like-minded individuals to gather once a month, share what’s captured their attention, discuss recent exploits or discoveries, and showcase projects born from curiosity or necessity. Whether it’s a half-finished experiment, a new idea sparked by a problem, or something ready for collaboration, this is a place to share and grow together. Most of all, this group encourages rediscovering that spark of curiosity — dusting off those badges, boards, and brainstorms — and diving once again into the spirit of exploration that brought us all here.

events.description:
​Leading Under Pressure

​How Stress, Communication & Leadership Behaviors Shape Cybersecurity Team Performance

​Cybersecurity leaders are expected to operate in high-pressure environments where constant escalation, incident fatigue, staffing strain, and nonstop communication demands have become normalized.

​But stress does not stay isolated to individuals.
It spreads through teams.

​The way leaders communicate during pressure — especially after incidents, mistakes, or prolonged overload — directly shapes psychological safety, team trust, engagement, and long-term performance.

​Leading Under Pressure is a highly interactive 4-hour workshop designed specifically for cybersecurity managers and team leaders who want to better understand:

  • ​how stress changes leadership behavior

  • ​how communication impacts team performance

  • ​how burnout silently propagates through organizations

  • ​how to build healthier, more sustainable cybersecurity teams

​This is not traditional leadership training.
It is a practical, psychologically intelligent operational leadership workshop grounded in the real-world realities of cybersecurity.

​Participants will experience:

  • ​realistic cybersecurity leadership scenarios

  • ​a proprietary leadership style assessment

  • ​communication-under-pressure exercises

  • ​burnout & stress awareness frameworks

  • ​practical recovery and sustainable performance strategies

  • ​facilitated peer discussion with other cybersecurity leaders

​Pilot workshops are intentionally limited to a small cohort of participants to encourage meaningful discussion, reflection, and feedback that will help shape future Green Shoe Consulting workshops and the GROE learning platform.

​Ideal for:
Cybersecurity managers, SOC leaders, IR managers, security engineering managers, and team leads responsible for both operational performance and people leadership.

​4 CPE / CEU eligible hours.

​Cost: $350 per attendee

​Cybersecurity leaders are expected to operate in high-pressure environments where constant escalation, incident fatigue, staffing strain, and nonstop communication demands have become normalized.

​But stress does not stay isolated to individuals.
It spreads through teams.

​The way leaders communicate during pressure — especially after incidents, mistakes, or prolonged overload — directly shapes psychological safety, team trust, engagement, and long-term performance.

​Leading Under Pressure is a highly interactive 4-hour workshop designed specifically for cybersecurity managers and team leaders who want to better understand:

  • ​how stress changes leadership behavior

  • ​how communication impacts team performance

  • ​how burnout silently propagates through organizations

  • ​how to build healthier, more sustainable cybersecurity teams

​This is not traditional leadership training.
It is a practical, psychologically intelligent operational leadership workshop grounded in the real-world realities of cybersecurity.

​Participants will experience:

  • ​realistic cybersecurity leadership scenarios

  • ​a proprietary leadership style assessment

  • ​communication-under-pressure exercises

  • ​burnout & stress awareness frameworks

  • ​practical recovery and sustainable performance strategies

  • ​facilitated peer discussion with other cybersecurity leaders

​Pilot workshops are intentionally limited to a small cohort of participants to encourage meaningful discussion, reflection, and feedback that will help shape future Green Shoe Consulting workshops and the GROE learning platform.

​Ideal for:
Cybersecurity managers, SOC leaders, IR managers, security engineering managers, and team leads responsible for both operational performance and people leadership.

events.description: OWASP New York City Chapter \*\*\* NOTE: Please register for the official event on Luma, where you will be able to view the Zoom meeting link and other details/updates. [https://luma.com/jfipvwg9](https://luma.com/jfipvwg9) Abstract: For decades, the cybersecurity industry has been caught in a "more is better" cycle—more tools, more alerts, and more complexity. Yet, despite mounting budgets, the "Very Sophisticated Wind Fallacy" persists: we often mistake simple architectural failures for unstoppable adversary genius. It’s time to stop trying to hear the signal through the noise and start silencing the noise at the source. In this session, Christopher Frenz introduces a shift from additive to Subtractive Security. Drawing from a 25-year career as a CISO and scientific researcher, he will present the first mathematical framework for complexity reduction. We will move past the "Illusion of the Magician" to focus on Path Erasure Rate (PER)—a metric that measures what an attacker cannot do rather than what we hope to detect. Key Takeaways: * **The Hero vs. Silent CISO:** Why our current auditing structures reward reactive firefighting over quiet, resilient environments. * **Architectural Erasure:** How to use IOAs, aggressive egress filtering, and web blocks to fundamentally shrink your attack surface. * **The Math of Less:** An introduction to the mathematical framework behind The Science of Silence and how to apply it to your AppSec program today.
